2609.31180.title: BAT-CLIP: Trimodal Alignment of Brain, Audio and Text
2609.31180.paper_summary: Decoding and interpreting naturalistic speech from the brain increasingly relies on alignment to pretrained speech and language representation spaces. However, current CLIP-style brain-speech alignment ground neural activity to a single anchor modality-audio or text-despite the brain's inherently multimodal speech processing. This induces a trade-off: audio anchoring preserves temporal structure but weakens linguistic separability, while text anchoring captures semantics yet discards acoustic detail. We propose BAT-CLIP, the first CLIP-style trimodal alignment framework for iEEG that jointly aligns neural embeddings to both pretrained audio and text anchors in a shared, frozen audio-text manifold. On the naturalistic Podcast benchmark, BAT-CLIP yields more robust representations than bimodal CLIP baselines. We also highlight the importance of using self-supervised foundation models for CLIP training.
2609.31180.paper_summary_zh: 解碼和解釋來自大腦的自然語音越來越依賴於與預訓練的語音和語言表示空間的對齊。<lb/>然而，當前的 CLIP 風格大腦-語音對齊將神經活動固定在單一的錨定模態——音頻或文本——儘管大腦本身具有多模態的語音處理能力。<lb/>這導致了一種權衡：音頻錨定保留了時間結構，但削弱了語言的可分性，而文本錨定則捕捉了語義卻丟棄了聲學細節。<lb/>我們提出了 BAT-CLIP，這是第一個 CLIP 風格的三模態對齊框架，用於 iEEG，該框架將神經嵌入共同對齊到預訓練的音頻和文本錨定，在共享的、固定的音頻-文本流形中。<lb/>在自然語音播客基準上，BAT-CLIP 產生的表示比雙模態 CLIP 基準更穩健。<lb/>我們還強調使用自監督基礎模型進行 CLIP 訓練的重要性。
